questions.stem: Which blood vessel has the thickest muscular wall?
questions.explanation: Arteries have the thickest muscular walls and elastic fibres to withstand the high blood pressure generated when the heart pumps blood and to maintain pressure between heartbeats.

options.text: To prevent the backflow of blood as it returns to the heart at low pressure

questions.explanation: Veins carry blood at low pressure back to the heart. Valves prevent blood from flowing backwards due to gravity, ensuring it keeps moving in the correct direction.

questions.stem: What makes capillaries ideal for substance exchange?

options.text: They have walls only one cell thick, allowing easy diffusion of substances
They have valves to control flow
They carry blood at very high pressure

questions.explanation: Capillary walls are only one cell thick (endothelium), providing a very short diffusion distance for oxygen, nutrients, carbon dioxide, and waste products to move between blood and tissues.

questions.stem: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. It is the only artery that carries deoxygenated blood.

questions.stem: Why do arteries have elastic fibres in their walls?

options.text: To make them flexible enough to stretch and recoil with each heartbeat, maintaining blood pressure

questions.explanation: Elastic fibres in artery walls allow them to stretch as blood is pumped through under high pressure and then recoil to help push the blood along, helping to maintain a steady blood pressure.

questions.stem: How does blood return to the heart through veins?

options.text: By the squeezing action of surrounding skeletal muscles, assisted by valves
By the pumping action of the heart alone

questions.explanation: Blood in veins is at low pressure. It is pushed back to the heart by the contraction of surrounding skeletal muscles, which squeeze the veins. Valves prevent backflow between squeezes.

questions.stem: What is the lumen of a blood vessel?

options.text: The inner hollow space through which blood flows

questions.explanation: The lumen is the central hollow space inside a blood vessel through which blood flows. Arteries have a narrow lumen, veins have a wider lumen, and capillaries have the narrowest lumen.
